newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.00/3.05 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.00/3.05 percent.

text.p: German call money rates remained mostly steady at about 3.00/3.05 percent in relatively quiet dealings ahead of the weekend.
Rates on Thursday had slipped to about 3.00/3.05 percent compared with 3.05 percent on Wednesday after the Bundesbank did not cut the repo rate despite some market speculation.
"There is not much going on in the market. It's been a relatively quiet day," said one Frankfurt trader.
Traders said liquidity was adequate for current conditions and expected call money rates to remain for the near-term close to the fixed-rate repo level of 3.00 percent.
Rates remained relatively steady despite the Bundesbank saying that commercial bank reserves fell to 38.7 billion marks as of Thursday from 39.8 billion marks on Wednesday.
But the monthly average rose to 37.6 billion marks from 37.5 billion marks, the German central bank said.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was also slightly lower at 3.05242 percent compared with 3.06167 percent on Thursday.
